title: What is the digital root of ten more than the number?
description: An eight digit number has digital root five, and we add ten to it. Ten is nine plus one, and adding nine does not change the digital root, so only the one counts. A check with one crore four confirms the new root.
teaching_notes: One idea: the digital root follows the remainder on division by nine, so adding ten changes the remainder by one. Watch for students who add ten to the digital root itself instead of using nine plus one.

video_script.why: A learner uses the link between the digital root and the remainder on division by nine to see what adding ten does to the root.
video_script.substitution: the book's own condition, an 8-digit number with digital root 5
video_script.anchor: an eight digit number with its digital root 5 and the same number plus 10
video_script.payoff_line: The digital root of the new number is six.

final_answer.spoken: the digital root of the new number is six

maths_rules: 10 = 9 + 1; adding 9 leaves the remainder on division by 9 unchanged; adding 1 raises it by 1
the digital root goes up from 5 to 6
check: 10000004 has 8 digits and digit sum 1 + 4 = 5, root 5; 10000014 has digit sum 1 + 1 + 4 = 6, root 6
video_script.design: One idea: ten is nine plus one, so the digital root rises by one. Assumes the link between the digital root and the remainder on division by nine. The two numbers stay on the board all video.

<bookmark mark='after'/>Ten more is one crore fourteen. Its digit sum is six, so its digital root is six.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The digital root of the new number is six.
